info.name: User Management System
info.description:
Every endpoint across the system: the two interchangeable product backends, and the
feature toggle service that decides who may use them.

RUN ORDER MATTERS. Folder 1 signs in as all three operators and stores their tokens;
everything after it depends on those variables. Folder 6 creates a feature the later
requests in that folder use, and deletes it at the end.

THREE BASE URLS:
  baseUrl    the product API   :8080 micronaut | :8082 spring boot | :8081 through nginx
  opsUrl     health / metrics  always a product backend, never the proxy
  featureUrl the feature service :8084 — it owns the toggles and the access rules

Safe to run repeatedly: created users and features carry a timestamp and are cleaned up.

item.name: 1 · Authentication
item.description: Signs in all three operators. Every later folder depends on these tokens.

request.description: Full access. Stores `adminToken`, which collection-level auth uses by default.

exec: pm.test('expires_in is seconds, not milliseconds', () => pm.expect(b.expires_in).to.eql(3600));
pm.test('roles carry ROLE_ADMIN and nothing internal', () => { pm.expect(b.roles).to.include('ROLE_ADMIN'); pm.expect(b.roles.join()).to.not.include('FACTOR_'); });

request.description: May read user data; refused every write and the toggle.

item.name: Sign in — operator with no access

request.description: Authenticates successfully and is refused everything. Authentication is not authorisation.

item.name: Unknown user is indistinguishable from a wrong password

request.description: Same status and same body — the response must not reveal whether the account exists.

exec: // Unique per run so re-running never trips the uniqueness rule.
pm.test('Location points at the new resource', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.include('/api/v1/users/'));
pm.test('createdAt is an ISO-8601 string, not a number', () => pm.expect(b.createdAt).to.be.a('string').and.match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T/));

request.description: Paged and sorted. `sort` accepts only firstName, lastName, email, createdAt, updatedAt.

exec: pm.test('content is always an array', () => pm.expect(b.content).to.be.an('array'));

item.name: List users — page beyond the end

request.description: An empty page still carries `content: []`. Omitting it would give clients null.
Case-insensitive substring across first name, last name and email.
Update replaces every editable field, so the omitted phone is cleared.

exec: pm.test('updatedAt moved past createdAt', () => pm.expect(new Date(b.updatedAt) >= new Date(b.createdAt)).to.be.true);

item.name: Server-managed fields are ignored, not rejected

request.description: BR-5: a client echoing back id/createdAt is ignored rather than refused.
BR-2: a field of only spaces trims to empty and fails @NotBlank.

item.name: 3 · Error contract
item.description: One envelope for every failure, and the documented status for each. Both product backends must answer identically — several of these were 500s until this folder existed.

request.description: Reuses the address folder 2 created. Uniqueness is enforced by ux_users_email_lower, so it holds under concurrency rather than relying on a check-then-insert.

item.name: Empty body reports every missing field at once

exec: pm.test('lists more than one field error', () => { const e = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(e.fieldErrors).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(e.fieldErrors.length).to.be.above(1); });

item.name: Unknown sort field is 400, never SQL

request.description: Sort fields come from an allow-list and are rejected before the query builder.
A path value that cannot be converted is the caller's mistake. This answered 500 until it was tested.
Deletion is deliberately unimplemented. Both backends answer 405, not 500.
Unauthenticated and forbidden are different answers; the UI branches on both.

item.name: Every failure carries a correlation id
4 · Role-based access
item.description: The product API asks the feature service whether the caller may act. Rules live there; these requests prove the product applies the answer.

request.description: Authenticated, but no role permits the user-data feature.

item.name: 5 · Feature service · runtime
item.description: What the proxy and the product backends ask for. These endpoints are the reason the service exists; administration is folder 6.

request.description: Active backend plus the caller's own rights, used by the product UI toolbar.
Anonymous by design: the proxy has no credentials. 204 with the upstream in a header.
What a product backend calls, forwarding the end user's token.

exec: pm.test('allowed, and not read-only', () => { pm.expect(b.allowed).to.be.true; pm.expect(b.readOnly).to.be.false; });
pm.test('is a decision, not a feature dump', () => pm.expect(b).to.have.all.keys('feature','allowed','readOnly','deniedMessage','allowedRoles'));
pm.test('200 OK — a decision, not a refusal', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Access decision — unconfigured feature is allowed

request.description: Absence of policy is not a refusal. Refusals come from a policy that exists and excludes the caller.
Takes effect on the next request — no restart, no redeploy.

item.name: 6 · Feature service · administration
item.description: Full CRUD over toggles, their role lists and their policy, plus the guardrails and the audit trail. Creates a feature at the start and deletes it at the end, so the folder is re-runnable.

exec: pm.test('protection is server-computed', () => { const p = b.find(f => f.uid === 'user-data-access'); pm.expect(p.isProtected).to.be.true; });

request.description: A created toggle does nothing until code reads it.

exec: // Unique per run so the folder can be re-run.
pm.test('new features are not protected', () => pm.expect(b.isProtected).to.be.false);
pm.test('roles and properties are present', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.roles).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(b.properties).to.be.an('object'); });

request.description: Granting and revoking are separate explicit actions, never a wholesale list save.
Policy the role list cannot express: read-only roles, who may administer, what to say when refusing.

exec: pm.test('property is stored', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().properties.deniedMessage).to.eql('Set by the Postman collection.'));

item.name: Duplicate create is 409, never an overwrite
GUARDRAIL — a protected feature cannot be deleted

request.description: BR-9. Deleting it would leave access to user data unconfigurable.
Allowed: a role remains that can still administer it.

item.name: GUARDRAIL — the last role cannot be removed

request.description: BR-8. This is the change that would lock every operator out of user data.
Leaves the ACL as it was found — these requests take it deliberately to the edge.

exec: pm.test('ACL is whole again', () => { const r = pm.response.json().roles; pm.expect(r).to.include('ROLE_ADMIN'); pm.expect(r).to.include('ROLE_VIEWER'); });

item.name: A read-only operator may list but not change
A read-only operator is refused a create
A no-access operator is refused even the listing

request.description: A refusal must reveal nothing about which toggles exist.
Append-only. Every change is recorded before it is applied, and refusals are recorded too.

exec: pm.test('entries carry who, what and when', () => { const e = b[0]; pm.expect(e.user).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(e.action).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(e.at).to.be.a('string'); });
pm.test('refused attempts are recorded too', () => pm.expect(b.some(e => e.action.endsWith('_REFUSED'))).to.be.true);
pm.test('newest first', () => { if (b.length > 1) pm.expect(new Date(b[0].at) >= new Date(b[1].at)).to.be.true; });
